minutes.headline: Parks Commission heard Marshall Park phasing update; cost decision on phases set for the Feb 19 meeting.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the recreation director on beach staffing, lifeguard hiring, February programs and the spring fair, then the chair on the revised Marshall Park phase layout ahead of town meeting. No formal votes beyond adjournment were captured; the phasing decision was deferred to Feb 19 and a Feb 5 workshop on park user fees was set.

budget_items.what_was_said: Scan counts by time of day show the busiest period is the morning, supporting more morning staffing.

budget_items.topic: Lifeguard pay step for WSI holders
budget_items.what_was_said: Possibility of starting lifeguards with water safety instructor certification at a higher step; HR to be consulted. WSI reimbursement process changed to direct deposit.
Family cap and per-person price set for the February 7 program, registration filling.
Petting zoo, bounce house and dunk tank are not covered by the town's normal insurance; vendors add the town to their certificates, and event coverage quotes may be needed.
Commission will seek funds at May town meeting for chosen phases; updated cost estimates due to the design team Feb 18; selectmen need the borrowing amount by Feb 20.

budget_items.topic: Board of Health funds for restroom septic
budget_items.what_was_said: Question whether the money could be used to connect to sewer instead of a new septic; the admin said no, written confirmation to be sought.
The skate park group is still trying to raise more money to finish financing.
February 5 workshop to review comparable communities' fees and the goal for fee revenue.

decisions.decision: Commission will decide Feb 19 whether to pursue phase one only, one plus 2A, or all phases for the town meeting borrowing article.
Announcer booths to be left out for now; utilities (power and water) to be run to the locations and capped for later booths.
Leaning toward adding one or two lights on the access drive from the main road.
Earth Day cleanup: keep the informal individual-participation approach as last year, with an idea to add something for younger children.
No action on master planning steering committee assignment; revisit if a need arises.
Special workshop on park user fees set for Feb 5; regular meeting Feb 19.
Facilities director to follow up with Board of Health and get written answer on use of the funds.

what_happened.line: The commission deferred its choice among phase one only, phase one plus 2A, or all phases of Marshall Park to its Feb 19 meeting.
The commission will seek funds at May town meeting; cost estimates are due to the design team Feb 18 and the borrowing amount to selectmen by Feb 20.
Announcer booths are left out for now, with power and water run to their locations and capped for later booths.
The commission was told restroom septic money from the Board of Health probably cannot be used for a sewer connection; written confirmation is to be sought.
A special workshop on park user fees was set for Feb 5, ahead of the regular Feb 19 meeting; no votes other than adjournment were taken.

why_it_matters: The phase chosen on Feb 19 sets the size of the borrowing article residents will be asked to vote on at May town meeting for Marshall Park.
The Feb 5 fee workshop could change what residents and families pay to use town parks and programs.
